_note: Processor Rep concession ladder (deterministic) and mock negotiation scripts. The rep's offers are terms; dollar figures are computed by src/finance. Mock text must agree with the ladder; tests/test_pipeline.py checks it.

hardball.label: Rep: IC+ 0.25% + $0.08, no monthly fees, exit clauses waived

diplomat.label: Rep: IC+ 0.30% + $0.10, no monthly fees, 12-month price lock

hardball: Maria is paying 3.28% all-in on $1.2M a year. Harbor Payments quoted interchange plus 0.20% and eight cents, month-to-month, free terminal. Your tier surcharges alone are $682 a month. Move her to interchange-plus today or we start the switch paperwork.
0.40% is still double the market. And let's talk about the 'regulatory' fee: no regulator charges it. Strip every monthly fee, get under 0.30%, and put it in writing.

Final ask: interchange plus 0.25% and eight cents, zero monthly fees, and you waive the liquidated damages and auto-renewal clauses. Yes by Friday, or she signs with Harbor and we file a complaint about the PCI fee practice.
diplomat: Mario's has processed with Keystone since last December and never had a chargeback problem. Maria wants to stay, but her margins are 3%. Can you show her a price that lets her keep you?

That's real progress, thank you. She's opening a weekend brunch service in spring, so that's more volume for you. If you can drop the batch fee and come down a little more, I think we can lock this in.
Interchange plus 0.30% and ten cents with no monthly fees and a 12-month price lock works for her. Can you confirm in writing and help her complete the PCI questionnaire this week?
rep_hardball: I hear you. I can move Mario's to interchange plus 0.65% and ten cents and waive the Customer Insights and statement fees. That's a significant improvement.
Okay. Interchange plus 0.40% and ten cents, and I'll drop the regulatory fee and statement fee. PCI stays until she validates.

Fine. Interchange plus 0.25% and eight cents, no monthly fees, and I'll get the liquidated damages and auto-renewal clauses waived in an amendment. I can't match Harbor's ten-dollar account fee structure, but I can do this.
rep_diplomat: We appreciate Maria's business. I can offer interchange plus 0.70% and ten cents and remove the Customer Insights and statement fees.
For a loyal account, interchange plus 0.45% and ten cents. I'll remove everything except the batch fee.
Interchange plus 0.30% and ten cents, no monthly fees, with a 12-month price lock. I'll send the SAQ link today.

referee_rationale: Hardball wins. The Harbor quote gave us real leverage, and the rep went to {hardball_label} with the exit traps waived. That's {hardball_annual}/yr with no switching costs. Switching to Harbor looked best on paper ({switch_annual}/yr), but the liquidated damages, ETF and lease buyout would cost {switch_one_time} up front, leaving Maria {switch_net_abs} {switch_net_word} after a year. Diplomat's deal is solid but leaves {hb_minus_dp}/yr on the table.
referee_reasoning_summary: Compared four paths on first-year net dollars from the calculator: stay as-is, Hardball deal, Diplomat deal, switch to Harbor. Switching only looks good before exit costs. Hardball beats Diplomat and also removes the liquidated-damages and auto-renew clauses, so Maria can walk next year if pricing creeps. Diplomat's 12-month lock is weaker than a consent requirement on fee changes.
